characters.summary: Willis Reed was a dominant, physical center and power forward for the New York Knicks known for his tenacious rebounding, inside scoring, and legendary toughness. He famously played through a severe thigh injury in Game 7 of the 1970 NBA Finals to inspire his team.
weaknesses: Knee and thigh injuries late in career

sources.supports: Career statistics, playing style, 1970 NBA Finals performance

feats.claim: Scored the first two baskets of Game 7 of the 1970 NBA Finals while playing on a torn thigh muscle, inspiring the Knicks to victory.

notableResults.note: Led the Knicks to series victories against Chamberlain's Lakers through team defense and clutch scoring.

unknowns: Exact blocked shot and steal statistics from early seasons as they were not officially recorded until the 1973-74 season.

characters.summary: Wilt Chamberlain was an athletic phenom and arguably the most statistically dominant center in basketball history, possessing unmatched strength, scoring capacity, and rebounding prowess. He scored 100 points in a single game and led the league in assists in 1968.
limitations: Low free-throw accuracy leading to intentional fouling strategies by opponents

sources.supports: 100-point game, career achievements, physical stats, and playstyle

feats.claim: Scored 100 points in a single regular-season game against the New York Knicks on March 2, 1962.
feats.citation: NBA regular season game, Hershey, Pennsylvania (1962)

feats.claim: Averaged 50.4 points per game during the 1961-62 NBA season.

notableResults.note: Frequent playoff matchups where Russell's Celtics usually defeated Chamberlain's teams.

unknowns: Unofficial quadruple-doubles in blocked shots prior to official recording.

characters.summary: Yao Ming was an elite, exceptionally tall center who combined enormous size with a soft shooting touch, exceptional passing vision out of the post, and high basketball IQ. His career was frequently hampered by lower-body injuries.
weaknesses: Susceptible to foot and ankle injuries due to extreme height and weight
Limited lateral quickness against small-ball lineups
limitations: Limited endurance due to heavy minutes and physical wear

sources.supports: Height, career statistics, playstyle, and injuries

feats.claim: Selected as an eight-time NBA All-Star and five-time All-NBA team member.

notableResults.note: Memorable head-to-head duels with high scoring output from both centers.

unknowns: Full potential limited strictly by chronic foot injuries.

characters.summary: Zion Williamson is an explosive, high-flying forward who combines massive size with elite speed, strength, and leaping ability. He excels as an interior slasher and transition threat capable of overpowering defenders in the paint.
weaknesses: Prone to lower-body and foot injuries
limitations: Periodic absences due to soft-tissue and foot injuries
